span.p: None acceptable

span.p: Coding worker or its command

span.p: Tests, verifier, dev server

span.p: Kernel installer

span.p: Vendor process, not its commands

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The boundary is the OS, not tool names. Every process an attempt starts runs sandboxed
Wrapped mode, the default: the whole vendor process tree runs in the sandbox
and keeps its native tools. Network: its provider and loopback MCP only
Logins: a client-supplied token or API key. Never a Claude subscription token
Stripped mode, the fallback: vendor shell off, harness.run over MCP,
file reads limited by its permission rules, subagents, hooks and web tools off
Our loop: harness.run and our edit tool. Codex: its own OS-enforced sandbox
Each harness.run gets its own Job Object. harness.start_service for servers
Wrapped agents have their own small cap. Everyone else shares a warm run pool
Conformance: .ssh unreadable by every native tool, non-provider web refused

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Strongest tier this PC can use

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Microsoft Execution Containers. No admin
Writes, secret reads and network enforced. Loopback allowed

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Two low-privilege users, once, with admin
ACLs plus firewall. Reads, writes and network enforced

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
No admin. Writes enforced. Secret reads are not
Network is advisory only. Yellow badge
Allowed only when the task needs no network and no untrusted code
Installs and dev servers need A, B or D
Foreign agents here: stripped mode only, Tier C tasks only

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Optional. Full enforcement, and Linux parity with CI

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Writable: this attempt's worktree, temp and build output
Read-only: toolchains, the package store, Git objects
Denied reads: .ssh, cloud creds, browser profiles, the vault area,
harness data, other worktrees, the developer's checkout
Only the kernel writes .git. Environment is scrubbed. HOME is inside the attempt
One Job Object: CPU, memory, process count, kill the tree
Wall-clock limits. A separate desktop where Windows supports it
A Job Object alone does not stop file or network access. The tier does

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Hold the task and explain. Never run unsandboxed in silence
An explicit project override shows a red banner on every card and receipt

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Who wants the network?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
No direct internet
harness.fetch_docs and harness.read_package_source only

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Loopback only, plus declared test hosts through an allowlisting proxy

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Package registries only, through the proxy

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: No direct internet. Doc fetcher, read-only, no side effects

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Its provider's API only

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Allowlisted docs and pinned READMEs. Strip scripts, hidden text
and invisible Unicode. Plain Markdown, size cap, cached by URL and hash
Returned as untrusted quoted material, with source and date
Prefer the installed package's own types and source
Workers do not browse: an injected page must not meet write access

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Workers never install. They send an intent. The integrator approves
The kernel installs with pnpm 10, whose scripts are blocked by default
A real build step is approved once and pinned. New packages are checked
for age, known vulnerabilities, typosquats and license
The lockfile is the only install source. npm and Yarn: scripts off,
then approved scripts run explicitly

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Text cannot grant power. Tools, paths, network and budget come from
the brief and the kernel. Context is labeled instruction, user, or data
Researchers read and cannot act. Workers act and do not browse
Every model output is schema-checked. Unknown actions are rejected
Diffs are scope-checked. Commands are allowlisted
harness.flag_blocked stops on a suspicious or contradictory instruction
The meta-lab plants injections and fake secrets and checks they are not followed

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Data folder is not readable by other users
Secrets stay in Credential Manager. Sandbox users cannot read DPAPI
Transcripts stay local. Raw audio is kept only if the developer turns it on
The redactor runs on logs, traces, diagnostics, exports and prompts
BitLocker is recommended. The database is not encrypted by the app in v1

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
What is protected: files outside the project, credentials, the checkout,
harness state and held-back tests, other attempts, accounts, and the plan
Who we assume: a confused model, injected text, a malicious package,
a malicious skill, or a worker editing tests

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A test that needs one host: the brief names it. The proxy allows that host
A network drive that cannot be ACL'd: tier A or D, or move the project
A missing tool: a human step or an approved toolchain install
A dev server binds loopback only, on a port for that attempt
Disabling the sandbox: red banner, recorded on every receipt

svg.text: Sandbox, network policy and what text cannot grant
